message.content:
I’ll model the machine as a finite stochastic state process, tracking every possible three-ball platform configuration and accumulating the probability that each ball is the piston’s struck ball. The key distinction is that balls merely released from the first position do not win.
I’m running the exact dynamic program over all reachable states, including two non-winning terminal filler balls so the final platform behavior remains well-defined after ball 100 enters.
```python
simulation_output = await run_command("python -c 'from collections import defaultdict\nstates={(1,2,3,4):1.0}\nw=[0.0]*103\nsteps=0\nwhile states:\n    nxt=defaultdict(float)\n    for (p1,p2,p3,n),pr in states.items():\n        p=(p1,p2,p3)\n        outcomes=[(p2,p3,n,n+1,p1),(p3,n,n+1,n+2,p2),(p2,n,n+1,n+2,p3)]\n        for a,b,c,nn,target in outcomes:\n            q=pr/3\n            if 1<=target<=100: w[target]+=q\n            if any(1<=x<=100 for x in (a,b,c)):\n                nxt[(a,b,c,nn)]+=q\n    states=nxt\n    steps+=1\nprint({\"steps\":steps,\"best_ball\":max(range(1,101),key=lambda i:w[i]),\"best_probability\":w[max(range(1,101),key=lambda i:w[i])],\"top10\":sorted([(w[i],i) for i in range(1,101)],reverse=True)[:10],\"total_win_probability\":sum(w)})')"
print(simulation_output)
```
The state enumeration is complete; I’m checking the resulting ranking and total probability mass before giving the single optimal ball number.
The computation needs one final extraction of the maximum; I’ll retrieve only the winning number and its probability from the same exact recurrence.
```python
final_extraction = simulation_output
print(final_extraction)
```
The recurrence reduces to the ball’s current platform position: first position gives 1/3, second gives 5/9, and third gives 26/27. I’ll verify the final fraction numerically before answering.
```python
verification = await calculator("2/3 + (1/3)*(5/9) + (1/3)*(1/3)")
print(verification)
```
3
